name: Nairobi
subtitle: Nairobi, capital of Kenya: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: Nairobi began in 1899 as a British camp and supply depot for railway construction workers on Maasai land.
Nairobi began as a railway camp for the Uganda Railway.

parts.text: Nairobi began in 1899 as a British camp and supply depot for railway construction workers on Maasai land.
Nairobi began as a railway camp for the Uganda Railway.
The name comes from a Maasai phrase meaning cool waters (spelled Enkare Nairobi in one source, Ewaso Nyirobi in another).
Nairobi's Maasai-phrase name is rendered as 'the place of cool water' (EBSCO spells it Ewaso Nyirobi; it also notes an earlier name, Mile 327).
Nairobi became capital of the British East Africa Protectorate in 1905.
Kenya's independence in 1963 made Nairobi the capital of the independent country.

blocks.prompt: About how many people do you think live in Nairobi?

parts.text: 4,397,073 in 2019, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Nairobi City County (county-level, not an urban-agglomeration figure), 2019 Kenya Population and Housing Census, census night 24 August 2019.

items.text: British build a camp and supply depot for railway construction workers on the site of Nairobi.
Nairobi becomes capital of the British East Africa Protectorate.
The museum that is now the Nairobi National Museum is officially opened as the Coryndon Museum (22 September).
During the Mau Mau uprising, Operation Anvil sweeps Nairobi and detains about 16,500 people, mostly Kikuyu.
Kenya becomes independent; Nairobi is its capital. The colonial-era museum is renamed National Museums of Kenya.
The bombing of the US Embassy in Nairobi severely affects the economy.
The Nairobi National Museum reopens in June after modernization that began in 2005.
